title: Candidate segmentation and sensitivity
intro: A02 teaches interpretable, testable candidate segmentation. Synthetic browser exercises are linked to a native TIFF pipeline and quantified real-world failures on BBBC038/039.

scientific_context.caution: BBBC038 fixed bright Otsu+watershed official test object F1 0.385. Passing a synthetic challenge does not establish accurate nuclei or exopher identification.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → independent Prove → delayed review; then compare multiple real TIFF configurations locally.

goals.title: Background subtraction and binary mask
goals.why: Unsigned numeric overflow or unreviewed background subtraction can corrupt candidate masks.
explain: Background correction must be explicit and performed in sufficient precision.
A threshold selects foreground pixels, not whole biological objects.

worked_example.code:
import numpy as np
raw=np.array([2,250,20],dtype=np.uint8)
print(np.maximum(raw.astype(float)-15,0))

goals.title: Filter small objects without silently merging
goals.why: The size filter can remove noise or erase meaningful small objects.
explain: Label connectivity and area units must be declared before interpreting counts.
A size threshold on connected objects is not a validated classifier.
Changing the threshold changes object counts and may bias biology.

worked_example.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
m=np.array([[1,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,0,0]],bool)
labels,n=ndi.label(m)
print('objects:',n,'pixel counts:',np.bincount(labels.ravel())[1:].tolist())

goals.title: Separate connected candidates using watershed seeds
goals.why: Touching nuclei may be undercounted, while inappropriate seeds cause oversegmentation.
explain: Marker-controlled watershed is sensitive to selected seeds and signal quality.
The distance transform describes separation from the background.
Seeds define object identities and can create false splits.

worked_example.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
m=np.array([[0,1,1,1,0],[0,1,1,1,0]],bool)
print('distances:',ndi.distance_transform_edt(m).round(1).tolist())

capstone.title: Generate traceable candidate objects
capstone.why: An end-to-end classical mask must preserve parameters, error cases and candidate status.
explain: Bright/dark rules alter segmentation dramatically; manual reference is needed for detection accuracy.
Use explicit strict foreground comparisons before connected labeling.
Size filtering is performed on connected components, not global pixel count.
